title: O COME, Thou Radiant Morning Star
description: O COME, Thou Radiant Morning Star in Tonic Solfa to SELENA, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 445.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to SELENA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: O COME, thou ra-diant morn-ing Star, A-gain in hu-man dark-ness shine! A-rise re-splen-dent from a-far! As-sert thy roy-al-ty di-vine! Thy sway o'er all the earth main-tain, And now be-gin thy glo-rious reign.

lines: O COME, thou radiant morning Star,
Thy sway o'er all the earth maintain,
And now begin thy glorious reign.
Thy kingdom, Lord, we long to see:
Thy sceptre o'er the nations shake!
Take (for thou didst their ransom find)
The purchased souls of all mankind.
Now let thy chosen ones appear,
Fly on the rebel sons of men,
Seize them with faith divinely bold,
And force the world into thy fold.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to SELENA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
